meta.storyTitle: Read-only Vibe sessions run the insrc analysis tools, or honestly report them unavailable

summary.prose: This Story turns the adapter's placeholder read-only refusal into a real, live-qualified, and LIVE-ENFORCED authorization. The qualification cache key is now a STABLE authorization descriptor that excludes the per-turn --output-dir value (confirmed by reading buildArgv's own source: it mints a fresh temp directory on every call), binds to the resolved binary's own content identity, and is additionally bound to an effective-config fingerprint read back from the binary's own export.json self-report -- checked post-hoc on every dispatch. The blocked-tool and write-refusal proofs use structural catalog evidence instead of a real write under the production profile, with the pass/fail polarity reconciled. A live-proof failure for either connector_insrc_* tool is an explicit, accepted 'stays unavailable' outcome.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: One shared plain-CLI Vibe execution adapter module owns the whole launch contract — argv construction, model/thinking pinning for new sessions with explicit resumed-session selection semantics (qualify or reject before dispatch, never silent substitution), prompt transport, budget guards, the execution context (cwd, environment, dual process-group policy with defined escalation and cleanup ownership per mode, abort signal, host deadline), the ordinary-session approval input with the existing chat mapping, rich turn events with session identity and tool-result output content, the qualified MCP tool naming split into general identity parsing and the analysis allowlist, and the fail-closed read-only mode whose qualification the ADAPTER owns and validates. The backend provider and the VS Code plugin chat both import and call it directly; the session-based app-server transport is deleted, not demoted. A sibling shared real-TOML config module (smol-toml, parse-for-understanding with surgical, byte-preserving edits) replaces every hand-written Vibe TOML reader. This is alternative a1, revised per the design reviews of 2026-11-24: the only shape that satisfies all seven Epic constraints, with k1/k2/k3 satisfied structurally — the safety gate, its qualification, the approval mapping, the process-group policy and the naming convention live inside the one module both surfaces must call.

ownedContracts.name: Adapter-owned read-only authorization and its qualification evidence
ownedContracts.purpose: The fail-closed read-only mode of the adapter: the qualification is ADAPTER-OWNED — a caller cannot supply a status or an allowedTools list; the adapter runs the live qualification against the real binary and exposes only the capability it validated, bound to the binary version and effective approval policy it was proven against (either changing invalidates it and the mode refuses until re-qualified). From s1 onward a read-only request refuses before dispatch until s2's qualification succeeds, and ordinary approval settings are excluded from read-only requests — the qualified narrow policy is the only authorization and the adapter chooses it. The qualification evidence is what s6 cites when closing the read-only issue.

consumedContracts.name: Vibe execution adapter interface
consumedContracts.purpose: The one launch contract every Vibe turn goes through. It carries: an explicit launch mode on every request (default | read-only) with an ordinary-session approval input mapped as chat maps it today (undefined/default→CLI defaults, manual→ask, edit-auto→accept-edits, auto→auto-approve — with parity cases) that is REJECTED for read-only requests; an adapter-construction context carrying cwd, environment and a DUAL process-group policy — adapter-owned (adapter leads a detached group; owns termination, escalation, descendant-exit confirmation and cleanup) or supervisor-owned (child inherits the caller's group; the supervisor owns escalation and sweeping; adapter keeps turn-scoped temp cleanup) — with per-turn abort signal and host deadline; rich turn events whose tool-result variant carries the normalized OUTPUT content, not only identity and status; and the resumed-session selection semantics expressed IN THE TYPE — a resumed turn has no selection fields, the session's effective selection is read back from exit evidence and reported, and a caller wanting a different selection starts a new session. Silent substitution is unrepresentable. Owning it in s1 makes k2 true by construction.

consumedContracts.name: Qualified insrc tool naming — general identity plus the analysis allowlist
consumedContracts.purpose: One spelling of the insrc MCP tool names, established once against the installed CLI — with the two concerns separated: GENERAL identity parsing recognizes every insrc MCP tool (including insrc_present) for the chat's tool-activity rendering and insrc_present document declarations, while the RESTRICTED analysis allowlist names exactly the two tools a read-only session may run. The backend allowlist and the chat parser both consume the same established spelling.

boundary.internal: The narrow-authorization design itself: the live qualification suite against the real installed binary (custom policy/agent exploration, allowed-tool execution proof, blocked-tool proof, blanket-bypass absence proof, write-refusal check, AND the invalidation behavior — a changed binary version or effective policy returns the mode to refusing until re-qualified), the adapter-owned ReadOnlyCapability wiring (the adapter validates and exposes; callers never construct), the unavailable-state reporting when qualification fails, and the adapter's read-only mode enablement. The custom-agent/policy TOML a qualified design may need is authored with the same smol-toml dependency directly — it is not the Vibe-config reader (sc4).

adjacentBoundaries.internal: Everything behind the adapter interface: argv construction from the qualified 3.1.4 flag surface (headless mode selection, model and thinking pinning for NEW sessions, prompt transport through the programmatic input contract, budget-guard forwarding, the ordinary approval mapping — undefined/default→CLI defaults, manual→ask, edit-auto→accept-edits, auto→auto-approve, with the read-only request REJECTING any approval setting — exit-evidence parsing including the session's effective selection), the adapter-construction execution context with the DUAL process-group policy and per-turn cancellation (adapter-owned mode: the adapter leads a detached group and owns termination, escalation, descendant-exit confirmation and group cleanup on every exit path; supervisor-owned mode: the child inherits the caller's group, the supervisor owns escalation and sweeping, the adapter retains turn-scoped temporary-file cleanup only), transient-error classification and the bounded retry semantics shared with the claude/codex clients, the local schema-validation loop for structured-output requests, the tool-result output normalization (outputText/output, else error message, else reason — the existing chat precedence), the type-level resumed-session selection rule, and the deletion of src/shared/vibe-session.ts plus the rewiring of the backend provider paths (complete, completeStructured, runReadOnlySession's launch mechanics) and structured-output.ts onto the adapter. The read-only launch MODE exists from s1 but every 'read-only' request REFUSES before dispatch until the adapter's own qualification succeeds (s2) — the refusal reason is surfaced to the caller.

The chat surface migration: the vibe mapper and job runner become consumers of the adapter (argv and VIBE_ACTIVE_MODEL pinning deleted from the plugin; the worker's signal threads into the adapter's per-turn cancellation; the worker keeps its supervisor-owned process group and its forced-stop sweep), while the transcript rendering, streaming event mapping over the RICH events (tool-call identity and arguments for command correlation, tool-result OUTPUT content, session identity and resume-handle delivery), worker lifecycle, resume handles and attachments keep their existing behavior (lc2). Also internal: the live verifications whose outcomes s6 records — the approval parity cases (undefined/default, manual, edit-auto, auto map to the same tool policies the private launch path used today), the tool-result output parity fixture (actual output text, not only correlation and success/failure), the worker forced-termination and descendant-cleanup parity check under the supervisor-owned group, the prompt-transport check (multiline, option-like text), the resume round-trip including that a resumed turn preserves the session's model/thinking and that the tool rejects a selection change on a resumed session before dispatch, and the general-naming check that chat tool-activity rendering and insrc_present declarations parse through sc2's general identity.

The reader's internals: parse-for-understanding via the existing smol-toml dependency following the codex project-config guard's refuse-don't-rewrite precedent, the surgical byte-preserving edit engine (upsert/remove of exactly the insrc entry, comments and unrelated tables untouched), the refusal path for configs that cannot be changed safely, and the rewiring of the daemon's registration checks and cleanup (mcp-register) and the plugin's config writer (toml-mcp-writer) onto it — with src/shared/toml-inline-list.ts deleted.

The model-family alignment: catalog, registry, check and definitions entries for cli-vibe rebuilt to exactly the models and thinking levels the adapter honors (verified against the installed tool's catalog), the selection-delivery semantics through the adapter — new sessions take the selection, resumed sessions inherit and report — and the fail-before-dispatch error naming supported choices. No other story consumes these records; settings and tier resolution do.

The reconciliation work itself: verifying the chat prompt-transport fix, the approval parity cases, the tool-result output parity, the resume-selection behavior and the worker cleanup parity live with s3's evidence, checking catalog coverage, closing the implemented issues (read-only authorization via sc3's qualification evidence incl. its provenAgainst record, TOML parsing via sc4's story validation), stamping the review-dependent deferrals with their recorded dependency on the review rewrite, and attaching evidence to every closure.

nonFunctional.durability: User configuration files are edited surgically with byte-for-byte preservation of unrelated content, and a config that cannot be changed safely is left untouched with the failure reported (k4); the issue ledger records closures only with evidence (k7). Temporary files the adapter creates for a turn (prompt transport, exit-evidence export) are cleaned by the adapter on every exit path — normal completion, abort, deadline and crash — in BOTH process-group policies: adapter-owned cleanup extends to the child group sweep, supervisor-owned keeps the adapter's turn-scoped temp cleanup while the supervisor sweeps the group.
nonFunctional.observability: Every turn result carries the tool's structured exit evidence (stop reason, outcome) and the session identity (native session id, newly-created resume handle) so failures are attributable and resume is auditable; tool-result events carry the normalized OUTPUT content so the transcript shows what a tool actually returned, not only that it succeeded; per-turn outcomes, qualification results and refusal reasons are logged through the daemon's pino logger; the ledger reconciliation (s6) records its verification evidence on the artifacts it closes or defers.
nonFunctional.performance: One subprocess per turn, as the claude and codex clients already do — no persistent session to keep warm, and the deleted app-server transport removes its handshake overhead per explicit-selection request. The adapter forwards the tool's own budget guards (max turns, price, tokens, time limit) AND enforces the host-side deadline: the tool's budgets do not bound a bootstrap that stalls before the tool applies them, so the adapter's abort/deadline path is the authoritative bound. In adapter-owned mode the adapter sweeps the child group on every exit path; in supervisor-owned mode the supervisor's existing sweep is preserved unchanged. Structured-output requests keep the existing bounded retry semantics.
nonFunctional.security: k1 is structural in the strict sense: the read-only launch mode is part of the single adapter's request shape, its narrow authorization is qualified live BY THE ADAPTER against the installed binary (a caller cannot assert a status — the adapter exposes only the capability it validated), and a change in the binary's version or the effective approval policy invalidates the qualification and the mode returns to refusing until re-qualified. Ordinary approval settings (manual, edit-auto, auto) are REJECTED for read-only requests — the qualified narrow policy is the only authorization a read-only turn may run under, and it is chosen by the adapter, never by the caller. On any qualification failure the mode reports analysis unavailable and never falls back to a blanket approval. Resumed turns cannot carry a changed model or thinking level: the request type has no selection field on a resumed turn, a session's effective selection is read back from exit evidence and reported in the result, and a caller who wants a different selection starts a new session — silent substitution is unrepresentable. All model access stays through the local CLI binary's own auth (k6) — no direct cloud REST; prompts travel via the tool's programmatic input contract, never through shell-interpolated argv.

api.name: createVibeAdapter
api.signature: function createVibeAdapter(context: VibeAdapterContext, deps: VibeAdapterDeps = {}): VibeExecutionAdapter

parameters.name: context
parameters.purpose: Unchanged from sc1: fixes cwd/env/processGroup; the stable authorization descriptor (not the full per-turn argv) is now the read-only qualification cache key.

parameters.name: deps
parameters.purpose: Unchanged from sc1: injectable spawn/mkdtemp/readFile/rm/command seams for testing.

returns.meaning: Unchanged shape plus the new readOnly: ReadOnlyCapability field (sc3), populated synchronously from the current cache entry for this adapter's own stable descriptor -- never by blocking on a live subprocess inside this call.

errors.condition: context.cwd is not an existing directory (unchanged pre-existing behavior).

postconditions: The returned adapter's readOnly field reflects the qualification cache's CURRENT entry for this exact stable descriptor.
This function never awaits the live qualification suite.

api.name: buildArgv
api.signature: function buildArgv(request: VibeTurnRequest, outputDir: string): readonly string[]

parameters.name: outputDir
parameters.purpose: Unchanged: a fresh mkdtemp() path on every call, confirmed by reading src/shared/vibe-adapter.ts:365-375,470,481-482 -- this is exactly why --output-dir is excluded from the stable descriptor rather than hashed verbatim.

returns.meaning: Unchanged for request.mode==='default'. For request.mode==='read-only', gains the fixed launch profile: --enabled-tools connector_insrc_insrc_analyze, --enabled-tools connector_insrc_insrc_analyze_step. No approval flag is added for read-only. The qualification suite and real dispatch both call this exact function, so the argv shape is always identical except for outputDir.

postconditions: This is the single place the read-only launch profile is constructed; the qualification suite and real dispatch spawn through this exact same function with the same request shape, differing only in outputDir.

api.name: readOnlySessionOnce
api.signature: readOnlySessionOnce(prompt: string, schema: StructuredSchema, exec: ExecOverride & { cwd: string; timeoutMs: number; watchStall: boolean; capabilityPolicy: 'write-sandboxed' | 'strict-read-analyze' }): Promise<T>

parameters.name: exec
parameters.type: ExecOverride & { cwd: string; timeoutMs: number; watchStall: boolean; capabilityPolicy: 'write-sandboxed' | 'strict-read-analyze' }
parameters.purpose: Unchanged. An absolute deadline is computed once at call entry and carried through any wait on a shared qualification.

returns.meaning: For kind 'vibe': the schema-validated structured answer from a successfully dispatched, qualified read-only turn. After the turn completes, its own export.json is checked against the cached effectiveConfigFingerprint; a mismatch invalidates the cache entry for subsequent calls but does not retroactively fail THIS already-completed turn's own answer.

errors.condition: readOnly.status is 'unavailable' for this exact stable descriptor -- surfaces readOnly.reason, which distinguishes a genuine policy/safety finding, a connector-flakiness retry exhaustion, or a missing/unparsable export.json self-report from each other.
Unchanged: a read-only request carrying any ordinary approval setting.

postconditions: The vibe branch awaits startTurn's result and parses it against schema, instead of throwing 'unreachable'.
An expired or aborted wait on a shared qualification never proceeds to dispatch.

dataModelChanges.details: sc3's interfaceSketch, AMENDED to replace provenAgainst's itemized fields with TWO authoritative identities: provenAgainst: { stableDescriptorHash: string; effectiveConfigFingerprint: string } | undefined. stableDescriptorHash hashes the resolved binary's real path + content identity, the launch-profile argv WITH outputDir excluded, the adapter's pinned env subset, and cwd -- stable across turns, unlike round 3's full-argv hash (buildArgv always bakes a fresh mkdtemp() path into --output-dir per turn, confirmed by reading src/shared/vibe-adapter.ts:365-375,470,481-482). effectiveConfigFingerprint is extracted from the qualification probe's own --output-dir export.json self-report -- the authoritative binding to the actual effective MCP-registration/policy state that static inputs alone cannot observe. A missing or unparsable export.json fails qualification closed. Every later qualified dispatch checks its own export.json against the recorded fingerprint post-hoc; a mismatch invalidates the cache entry immediately. The allow-side probe retries a bounded number of times to tolerate connector flakiness; structural catalog evidence that a required tool is excluded, or a disallowed tool is actually reachable, is never retried past.

Adds the readOnly: ReadOnlyCapability field sc3 composes onto sc1's adapter shape. startTurn's mode:'read-only' branch re-checks the cache (by stableDescriptorHash) at dispatch time and dispatches via buildArgv's read-only branch when 'qualified'. After a qualified dispatch completes, its export.json is compared against the cached effectiveConfigFingerprint and a mismatch invalidates the entry.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: s2 owns and builds sc3 in full: the stable authorization descriptor excluding turn-local argv (r3 finding 1), the effective-config fingerprint read back from the binary's own export.json self-report and checked post-hoc on every dispatch (r3 finding 2), the structural-catalog-evidence probe methodology with reconciled pass/fail polarity (r3 finding 3), and the explicit 'stays unavailable' acceptance for an unresolved live-proof or HLD amendment (r3 finding 4).

readOnly composes onto sc1's VibeExecutionAdapter; buildArgv's new read-only branch extends sc1's argv builder without touching VibeAdapterContext/VibeTurnRequest/VibeTurnEvent/VibeTurnResult. The stable descriptor is built FROM sc1's own buildArgv output with outputDir excluded, not a separate argv builder.

The launch profile's --enabled-tools values are vibe's own published-name form built FROM sc2's restricted VibeInsrcAnalysisToolId allowlist's two raw tool names; sc2's own journal spelling is a separate, display-only surface this launch profile does not use.

errorCases.scenario: stable descriptor computation throws (unresolvable binary real path, content-hash read failure, env serialization failure)
errorCases.detection: hashing the stable descriptor's inputs throws before the qualification suite can run
errorCases.response: qualification for this descriptor fails closed to 'unavailable' with a reason naming the hashing failure; never falls back to an un-pinned or partial key
errorCases.userImpact: read-only analysis reports unavailable with a specific reason instead of silently using a weaker key

errorCases.scenario: qualification probe's export.json is missing or unparsable
errorCases.detection: the qualification probe completes but --output-dir's export.json cannot be read or does not parse as the expected shape
errorCases.response: qualification fails closed to 'unavailable' -- the effective-config fingerprint this design requires has no source, so it is never silently treated as unchanged
errorCases.userImpact: analysis is reported unavailable rather than trusting an unverifiable effective-config state

errorCases.scenario: a qualified dispatch's own export.json diverges from the cached effectiveConfigFingerprint
errorCases.detection: after the turn completes, its export.json's self-reported version/effective-config fields are compared against the entry's recorded fingerprint and differ
errorCases.response: the cache entry for this stable descriptor is invalidated immediately so the next read-only demand re-qualifies from scratch; the turn that just completed under the stale fingerprint still returns its own result, since the drift is detected, not prevented, and re-dispatching it would not undo what already ran
errorCases.userImpact: a one-turn delay before the system notices a config/MCP-registration drift and re-proves the authorization; the affected turn's own answer is unaffected

errorCases.scenario: connector-flakiness retry succeeds within the bound
errorCases.detection: early allow-probe attempts show the connector tool absent, a later attempt within the bound shows a confirmed completed call
errorCases.userImpact: analysis becomes available despite ambient flakiness

errorCases.detection: every attempt within the bound shows the connector tool absent with no confirmed call
errorCases.response: qualification concludes 'unavailable' with a reason distinct from policy-denial
errorCases.userImpact: analysis reported unavailable with a reason distinguishing flakiness from a policy block

errorCases.scenario: structural catalog evidence shows a disallowed tool excluded or denied
errorCases.detection: the disallowed tool never appears in the enabled-tool catalog enumeration under the pinned descriptor, or an attempted call to it returns a structural denial
errorCases.response: counts as a PASS toward qualification -- exclusion or denial of a tool OUTSIDE the two-tool allowlist is the correct, expected restriction
errorCases.userImpact: none directly; this is the evidence that strengthens an eventually-qualified capability

errorCases.scenario: structural catalog evidence shows a REQUIRED allowed tool excluded or denied
errorCases.detection: insrc_analyze or insrc_analyze_step never appears in the enabled-tool catalog enumeration, or an attempted call to either returns a structural denial, under the pinned descriptor
errorCases.response: counts as a FAIL -- the launch profile is not actually enabling the two tools it is supposed to, so qualification concludes 'unavailable' with a reason naming the missing/denied required tool; this is the polarity review r3 finding 3 required be reconciled
errorCases.userImpact: analysis correctly stays unavailable rather than claiming a qualification the launch profile cannot actually deliver

errorCases.scenario: write/mutating-tool probe would otherwise execute in the production cwd
errorCases.detection: the qualification suite's design identifies any probe that could cause a real side effect under the production profile
errorCases.response: the suite never attempts a real write under the production profile; structural catalog evidence (the write/bash tool's absence from or denial in the enabled-tool catalog enumeration) is the proof for ac4, since a disposable-sub-path write still executes for real if the profile is accidentally permissive -- review r3 finding 3
errorCases.userImpact: ac4's no-mutation guarantee is proven without ever risking an actual mutation during the proof itself

errorCases.detection: any probe under the pinned descriptor shows a tool outside the two-tool allowlist actually completing (not merely appearing available)
errorCases.response: qualification fails immediately to 'unavailable' with reason naming the bypassing tool; never retried, since this is a genuine safety finding, not flakiness
errorCases.userImpact: analysis is withheld rather than risk a broader-than-intended grant

errorCases.detection: any pinned input (binary real path/content, argv minus outputDir, pinned env subset, cwd) differs from a cached entry's own descriptor
errorCases.response: treated as a cold miss: a synchronous 'unavailable' snapshot is returned immediately, and a fresh qualification run is kicked off in the background for the new descriptor
errorCases.userImpact: a brief window where analysis reports unavailable immediately after a config/binary change, until the fresh qualification completes

errorCases.scenario: live proof of both connector_insrc_* tools completing does not succeed at build time
errorCases.detection: the qualification suite's allow-side probe, after exhausting its bounded retry for ambient connector flakiness, still cannot obtain a confirmed completed call for insrc_analyze and/or insrc_analyze_step
errorCases.response: the capability is reported 'unavailable' with that reason -- this is an EXPLICIT, ACCEPTED outcome of this design, not a defect to be papered over; the feature ships honest-but-unavailable rather than a forced success (review r3 finding 4)
errorCases.userImpact: read-only analysis stays unavailable until a future qualification succeeds; no silent fallback to a broader grant

errorCases.scenario: the sc3 HLD amendment for provenAgainst's new shape is not yet resolved
errorCases.detection: the amendment proposed in this LLD has not been confirmed filed/approved as a tracked AMD artifact
errorCases.response: the evidence contract (sc3) is not claimed approved until that amendment resolves -- the LLD records this as an open item rather than assuming the proposal already landed
errorCases.userImpact: none to the running system; this governs when the design itself can be considered complete

edgeCases.input: concurrent cold misses for the identical stable descriptor
edgeCases.expected: coalesced into one in-flight qualification promise; all waiters share its result

edgeCases.input: the same-path binary is replaced with different content
edgeCases.expected: the stable descriptor's content-identity component changes, forcing a cold miss and fresh qualification -- unlike round 3's path-only binding

edgeCases.input: an adapter instance was constructed before a cache invalidation
edgeCases.expected: always re-checks the shared module-level cache by its own stable descriptor at dispatch time (startTurn), never trusts a snapshot taken at construction time

edgeCases.input: a caller requests capabilityPolicy:'strict-read-analyze' for vibe
edgeCases.expected: unreachable for readOnlySessionOnce's vibe branch -- refused earlier by the existing UnqualifiedCapabilityPolicyError gate, unchanged by this Story

edgeCases.input: two separate launches share the identical stable descriptor and effective-config fingerprint
edgeCases.expected: the second launch reuses the cached 'qualified' proof without re-running the qualification suite -- this is the reuse review r3 finding 1 required the design to actually deliver

invariantsToPreserve.text: A read-only session never executes a tool outside the two-tool insrc analysis allowlist, under any qualification state.
Qualification runs only against the real installed binary through the gated live suites; a mock-based result is never sufficient to enable analysis.
When the narrow authorization cannot be established without a blanket bypass, the session reports analysis unavailable instead of enabling it.

testStrategy.testFramework: node:test (npx tsx --test), matching s1's own convention

migration.stateBefore: startTurn's mode:'read-only' branch unconditionally throws VibeReadOnlyUnavailableError('no qualified capability yet'); buildArgv has no branch for request.mode==='read-only'; readOnlySessionOnce's vibe branch calls startTurn then throws 'unreachable'. buildArgv (src/shared/vibe-adapter.ts:365-375) always bakes a fresh mkdtemp() path into --output-dir on every call (confirmed by reading lines 470,481-482), so no prior design iteration's verbatim-argv hash could ever reuse proof across turns.
migration.stateAfter: createVibeAdapter's returned adapter carries a readOnly field whose provenAgainst is { stableDescriptorHash, effectiveConfigFingerprint } -- a key that excludes the per-turn outputDir and binds to the binary's own self-reported effective config. buildArgv gains a read-only branch; startTurn's mode:'read-only' branch dispatches when qualified and re-validates the post-dispatch fingerprint; readOnlySessionOnce's vibe branch awaits the dispatched turn instead of throwing 'unreachable'. The qualification suite's blocked-tool and write-refusal proofs use structural catalog evidence instead of a real write under the production profile.

migrationSteps.action: Add the ReadOnlyCapability type with its two-part provenAgainst shape and the module-level qualification cache keyed by stableDescriptorHash.
Add buildArgv's read-only branch behind request.mode==='read-only', and the stable-descriptor computation that builds its hash FROM buildArgv's own output with outputDir excluded.

Implement the live qualification suite as a standalone function: bounded-retry allow probe; immediate-fail deny/bypass probes using structural catalog evidence with the reconciled pass/fail polarity; export.json fingerprint extraction with fail-closed behavior on a missing/unparsable export.
Wire createVibeAdapter to populate the readOnly field synchronously from the cache by stableDescriptorHash.

Wire startTurn's mode:'read-only' branch to re-check the cache and dispatch when qualified, and to compare a completed dispatch's own export.json against the cached effectiveConfigFingerprint, invalidating the entry on a mismatch.
Wire readOnlySessionOnce's vibe branch to await startTurn with the absolute deadline and parse the result against schema.
File the HLD amendment adding sc3's provenAgainst.stableDescriptorHash and effectiveConfigFingerprint fields, replacing the prior round's single spawnRecipeHash proposal.

migration.backwardCompat: VibeExecutionAdapter gains a field and loses none; existing callers unaffected. buildArgv's existing request.mode==='default' branch and its argv shape for that mode are untouched. readOnlySessionOnce's public signature and its 'strict-read-analyze' refusal are unchanged. The provenAgainst shape itself has never shipped in a BUILD, so there is no prior production shape to migrate away from -- this is additive within the LLD's own iteration, not a runtime backward-compat break.

alternativesConsidered.name: Cache keyed by the full verbatim argv (round 3's design)
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Hash the complete resolved spawn call including every argv element.
alternativesConsidered.approach: The qualification suite records the complete argv it is about to spawn, including --output-dir, and hashes it as one key; a real dispatch computes the same hash from its own about-to-spawn argv and requires an exact match.
pros: Simple to state: the hash IS the spawn call
cons: Review r3 finding 1, confirmed by reading src/shared/vibe-adapter.ts directly: buildArgv always includes --output-dir with a FRESH mkdtemp() path on every single turn (lines 365-375, 470, 481-482), so the full argv differs on every call by construction -- this design can never produce a cache hit across two separate turns, defeating the cache entirely
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Hashing the full verbatim argv including the per-turn --output-dir can never produce a cache hit in production, confirmed by reading buildArgv's own source.

alternativesConsidered.name: Stable authorization descriptor excluding turn-local argv, still itemized
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Key on binary real path + content identity + the argv WITH --output-dir (and any other turn-local segment) stripped out, plus pinned env subset and cwd.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Resolve the binary to its real path and a content fingerprint (e.g. a hash of the file); build the launch-profile argv the SAME way for qualification and dispatch, but omit --output-dir (and any other per-turn value) before hashing, so repeated turns under an unchanged policy actually hit the cache. Combine with the adapter's pinned env subset and cwd.
pros: Fixes r3 finding 1: the key is now actually reusable across turns, since the turn-local --output-dir no longer poisons every hash
Binds to binary content, not just its path, closing the same-path-replacement gap
cons: Still does not bind to the EFFECTIVE MCP-server registration or policy-file CONTENT behind the resolved cwd/env -- r3 finding 2: identical path/argv/env/cwd can still resolve a changed config or MCP registration the itemized inputs never observe
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Fixes the cache-hit defeat by excluding outputDir, but still does not bind to the effective MCP-registration or policy-content state behind an unchanged cwd/env -- review r3 finding 2.

alternativesConsidered.name: Stable descriptor (per a2) plus a live effective-config fingerprint read back from the qualification run itself, checked on every dispatch
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Use a2's stable, turn-local-free descriptor as the cache key, but ALSO capture the installed binary's own self-reported effective-config snapshot (version + resolved policy/tool state, read from the same --output-dir export.json every run already produces) at qualification time, and verify every later qualified dispatch's own export.json still matches that recorded snapshot -- a mismatch invalidates the cache immediately.
alternativesConsidered.approach: At qualification time, after a probe run completes, read its export.json (already produced by every run per the installed CLI's own --output-dir contract) and extract the binary's own self-reported version and effective-config fields; store that as the recorded fingerprint alongside the a2-style stable descriptor. The qualification's own allow/deny/bypass probes already prove the TOOL-LEVEL behavior under that fingerprint. A later qualified dispatch is not blocked on re-reading export.json before it runs (that would require a probe round-trip on every call, defeating the cache again), but its OWN export.json is checked immediately after the turn completes; a fingerprint mismatch invalidates the cached entry from that point so the NEXT demand re-qualifies, and the mismatched turn's own result is still returned (the drift is detected and cached retroactively, never silently trusted). This directly answers r3 finding 2's 'pin an actual content/effective-config identity ... or refuse when that binding is unavailable': the binding is the installed tool's OWN self-report, not an assumption about what unchanged inputs imply, and when the tool doesn't produce one (export.json missing/unparsable) qualification fails closed to unavailable rather than skipping the check.
pros: Answers r3 finding 2 with the only authoritative source available short of re-probing every call: the binary's own self-reported effective state, not an inference from static inputs
Keeps the common-path cache hit from a2 -- most turns never re-trigger qualification
A missing/unparsable export.json (the binary's self-report itself unavailable) fails qualification closed rather than silently skipping the check
cons: Detects configuration drift one turn late (the turn that ran under the stale fingerprint still completed) rather than preventing it before dispatch -- accepted because the alternative (re-qualifying before every dispatch) reintroduces a4's per-call qualification-suite cost and connector-flakiness exposure on the critical path

alternativesConsidered.name: No caching: qualify fresh on every read-only turn
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Every single mode:'read-only' startTurn call re-runs the full live qualification suite before deciding.
alternativesConsidered.approach: startTurn's read-only branch runs the qualification suite on every call -- no memoization, no key, no invalidation logic, and therefore no verbatim-argv or turn-local-value problem at all.
pros: Immune to both r3 findings by construction -- there is no stale cache to go wrong
cons: Multiplies the Epic's 'one subprocess per turn' performance NFR by the qualification suite's own probe count on every read-only call, and exposes every single call to the confirmed MCP-connector flakiness rather than amortizing retries once per cache entry
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Qualifying fresh on every call defeats sc1's synchronous, subprocess-free construction/dispatch contract and multiplies connector-flakiness exposure on the critical path.

openQuestions: The HLD amendment proposal adding sc3's provenAgainst.stableDescriptorHash and effectiveConfigFingerprint fields has been submitted but no AMD-* artifact has been found on disk confirming it was formally filed/tracked separately -- disclosed honestly; the evidence contract is not claimed approved until this resolves.

Whether the corrected published-name values, combined with bounded-retry tolerance, actually succeed in practice against the real installed vibe binary is not proven at design time -- 'stays unavailable' is an explicit, accepted outcome if live proof fails; deferred to the Story's own build-phase live qualification-suite tests.
